purpose: Initial cross-domain People records showing how religious, occult, political, cultural and institutional communities can overlap. These are relationship seeds, not demographic estimates.

records.interpretation: A self-identified modern Satanist religious organization; individual members should not be assumed to share a single political program.
records.evidence_note: Use organizational self-description alongside scholarly treatments of modern Satanism; distinguish the organization from the wider category of Satanism.

records.interpretation: A modern religious organization whose public activity includes ritual, identity and political/legal advocacy; support for particular campaigns must be measured rather than generalized to all members.
An initiatory religious/esoteric community associated with modern Setian thought; distinguish its members from all people interested in Set symbolism.
A degree-based initiatory organization associated with Thelema and ceremonial/ritual traditions; membership is an institutional relationship, not an ethnicity or nationality.

records.preferred_name: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn community

relations.practices: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn

records.interpretation: A late-19th/early-20th-century occult order whose members formed a network of lodges and ritual practitioners; do not treat all occultists as Golden Dawn members.
A broad family of fraternal organizations with jurisdictional variation; lodge membership is the relevant institutional relationship and does not determine a member's religion or politics.
A transnational esoteric movement whose members may combine Theosophical ideas with other religious and cultural identities.

A movement around Rudolf Steiner's Anthroposophy with institutions and practices in education, agriculture, arts and spiritual study; participation in one field does not imply participation in all others.

A historical analytical category covering distinct anti-religious campaigns and organizations; it is not a single worldwide people and should be split by country, institution and period when evidence permits.
Project-defined contemporary symbolic/religious community. Its self-description and mythology are part of the project corpus and must remain distinct from externally measured demographic categories.

graph_rule: These records demonstrate cross-domain coupling. Each community can connect to country presence, religion, ideology, culture, institution, language, migration and history independently. No edge should imply that every member shares every connected attribute.
next_expansion: Replace seeds with country-by-country documented communities, historical populations, denominations, parties, cultural groups, occupational groups and diasporas; retain time-bounded evidence for every edge.
